title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Mercer customs, ceremonies, songs, and symbols tied to the University’s Macon heritage.

cards.title: Pilgrimage to Penfield
cards.subtitle: Annual visit to Mercer’s original campus
cards.notes: Join the fall trip to Penfield to see the original chapel, early academic-building foundation, cemetery, student presentations, and re-enactments.
cards.short_summary: Students commemorate Mercer’s 1833 beginnings at its original Greene County campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer says hundreds of students, including the first-year class, make this fall pilgrimage and that activities include a picnic, fireworks, presentations, and historical re-enactments.
cards.access_notes: University-organized fall tradition; participation details vary by year.

cards.title: The Jesse Mercer Good-Luck Rub
cards.subtitle: Jesse Mercer statue, Macon campus
cards.notes: Spot the founder’s bench statue during Convocation or Baccalaureate, when students traditionally rub his head for good luck before the next chapter.
cards.short_summary: A statue-head rub marks both the beginning and close of many students’ Mercer careers.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer documents the custom of first-year students rubbing Jesse Mercer’s head during Convocation and seniors doing so again at Baccalaureate for luck beyond Mercer.
cards.access_notes: View the statue from public campus walkways; ceremony participation is tied to University events.

cards.entity_name: Climbing the Godsey Administration Building Tower
cards.title: Signing the Tower
cards.subtitle: Godsey Administration Building, Macon campus
cards.notes: During the approved orientation trek, climb the building’s ladders and stairs to the tower and add your name and graduation year where directed.
cards.short_summary: For nearly a century, Mercer students have left signatures on the route to the tower.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer states that students have climbed the Godsey tower and left signatures for almost 100 years, with many signing as first-years.
cards.access_notes: Use only University-authorized access, typically offered as part of new-student programming.

cards.title: Homecoming’s Fall Finale
cards.subtitle: Homecoming Week, Mercer University
cards.notes: Follow the Homecoming Week schedule for student activities, pep rally, fireworks, alumni events, awards, and the football game.
cards.short_summary: Mercer’s fall Homecoming tradition builds to a weekend of campus and alumni events.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer says Homecoming Week includes student activities and culminates with a pep rally, fireworks, alumni events, awards, and the Homecoming football game.
cards.access_notes: Event access and ticketing vary by activity; consult the annual Homecoming schedule.

cards.title: Founders’ Day Return
cards.subtitle: Annual Mercerian speaker tradition
cards.notes: Attend the annual program to hear an invited Mercerian reflect on how the University shaped their life and connection to its history.
cards.short_summary: A revived heritage day brings a notable Mercer alum or community member back to speak.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer reports that the Student Government Association revived Founders’ Day in the mid-1990s and now invites a prominent Mercerian annually to speak.
cards.access_notes: Annual program; check University announcements for the speaker and venue.

cards.title: Light the Mercer Tree
cards.subtitle: Willingham Hall or its grounds
cards.notes: Gather for Mercer Singers carols, a University Minister meditation, a faculty reading, then the tree lighting with cookies and hot chocolate.
cards.short_summary: SGA’s holiday gathering combines music, readings, and a campus tree-lighting ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer says the Student Government Association hosts this annual tradition, ending with the Mercer Christmas tree lighting and cookies and hot chocolate.
cards.access_notes: Annual seasonal event; location may be Willingham Hall or the surrounding grounds.

cards.title: Meet Toby and Tot
cards.subtitle: Mercer’s named bear mascots
cards.notes: Look for Mercer’s bear mascots at University spirit events and learn the student newspaper contest that gave Toby his name in 1949.
cards.short_summary: Mercer’s male and female bear mascots have student-selected names with campus-history roots.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer states that students voted in a 1949 Cluster contest to name the bear mascot Toby and assigned Tot to the female bear mascot.
cards.access_notes: Mascot appearances depend on the event schedule.

cards.title: Orange and Black, Officially
cards.subtitle: Mercer school colors
cards.notes: Wear orange and black for campus spirit occasions, and connect the color pairing to the University’s official visual identity and Bear tradition.
cards.short_summary: Orange and black are the documented colors behind Mercer’s Bear identity.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer identifies orange and black as its school colors in its official campus traditions history.
cards.access_notes: A school-symbol tradition rather than a scheduled event.

cards.title: Sing the Mercer Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: University song tradition
cards.notes: Learn the Alma Mater before a major University gathering so you can recognize its refrain and join in when the occasion calls for it.
cards.short_summary: Mercer preserves the full Alma Mater as one of its named campus traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s official traditions page publishes the lyrics and identifies them as the Mercer Alma Mater.
cards.access_notes: Song participation is associated with University ceremonies and gatherings.

cards.title: Ring Out the Victory Song
cards.subtitle: Mercer Fight Song
cards.notes: Listen for the fight song at Bear spirit occasions and follow its orange-and-black refrain as part of Mercer’s shared athletic tradition.
cards.short_summary: The University documents its fight song alongside its other defining customs.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s official traditions page publishes the Mercer Fight Song, including its refrain and chorus.
cards.access_notes: Song participation is associated with University and athletics spirit events.
